messages:
anita: Quick heads-up, q4b-int4 (cuda-opt) pass@1 on the codebench dropped from 42% -> 27% after the latest quant run. Repro on CI. Anyone else seeing code-gen regressions?
marco: Yikes. Which commit/quant flags?
anita: commit 0b9f2d, quant flags: --bits 4 --group 256 --perchannel. Hosted q8b baseline still at 41%.
rachel: I pulled the bench run. Breakdown: python tasks/codebench/run_eval.py --model q4b-int4 --suite code-synth --seed 42
Results summary: {"pass@1":"27%","pass@5":"46%","compilation_errors":"3.4%","syntax-hallucinations":"7.2%"}
marco: 7.2% hallucinations is annoying. Any pattern on prompt types? short snippets vs long?
tom: Could be tokenization/indent normalization or dedupe artifacts in the golden set. If a golden example was deduped or migrated with a different normalizer it can change ground-truth formatting.
anita: I ran a diff on golden examples used by codebench: ./tools/golden_diff.py --old golden_v12.json --new golden_v13.json --out diffs.csv
Count: total_golden=1200, changed=84 (7%), formatting-only=52, semantic-change=32
marco: 32 semantic changes could explain some regressions. Any examples?
rachel: sample of 3 failing cases uploaded: https://internal.storage/redwood/codebench/fail-samples-1790012345.tar.gz
Included: one-liner lambda refactor -> normalized to multiline in new golden -> model now fails exact-match.
tom: For code evals we should tolerate whitespace/formatting diffs. Suggest pipeline change: use AST-based equivalence for python tests instead of strict text match. Also: pause auto-golden refresh for codebench until we confirm.
curation-bot: Golden set update paused for pipeline codebench-eval by eng-ml (reason: q4b-int4 regression triage) until 2026-03-25T08:00Z.
label-ops: We can take a quick relabel batch. Recommend freeze 100 examples flagged as semantic-change and 50 edge-format-only for manual review. Tagging queue: code-quant-regress/priority.
anita: Plan proposal:
- create diagnostic sample: 300 code prompts (mix: python snippets, js, sql) pulled from seedbank with high-change score
- freeze 100 semantic-change golden (send to label-ops)
- run AST-equivalence diffs for python and structural compare for js/sql (tooling: tools/code_equiv.py)
- run eval matrix: hosted-q8b vs q8b-int4 vs q4b-int4 -> record pass@1, pass@5, exact-match relaxed, AST-match
- if q4b-int4 still lags on AST-match by >10% we rollback quant flags and open quant-bisect

marco: I'll spin the eval matrix: ./scripts/eval_matrix.sh --models hosted-q8b,q8b-int4,q4b-int4 --suite code-synth --out matrix-1790012345.json (ETA 2h)
rachel: I'll prepare the frozen golden + CSV of 32 semantic-change examples and add notes for label-ops.
label-ops: Acknowledged. We can start relabel within 12h. Expect ETA 36h for full 150-item batch.
tom: Small CI change request: add AST-equivalence check as a post-processor for codebench and report both exact and AST pass rates.
anita: Also, recording a short repro: failing prompt id 41321, input: "def sum(a,b): return a+b" expected single-line output vs model now emits trailing comment + different whitespace. Attached in the archive.
marco: uploaded eval matrix and preliminary diff stats to https://internal.storage/redwood/evals/matrix-1790012345.json and logs at /tmp/code-reg-1790012345.log
curation-bot: Ticket created: CTC-1432 "q4b-int4 codebench regression triage + golden freeze" assigned to anita, marco, rachel.
rachel: Quick note: also seeing slight increase in near-duplicate prompts in ingests (seedbank overlap) after dedupe param tweak last week. I'll run a de-dupe overlap check and share counts.
anita: Good catch. If upstream de-dupe changed, that could alter sample distribution and surface new edgecases in codebench.
marco: Action items recap:
- marco: run eval matrix + share artifacts (due +2h)
- rachel: prepare frozen golden 150 and de-dupe overlap report (due +4h)
- label-ops: relabel 150 (ETA 36h)
- tom: add AST postprocess to CI (follow-up PR)
- eng-ml: hold auto-golden refresh for codebench until checks complete
anita: thanks all. I'll monitor infra runs and bump if we see further drift. :eyes:
